classification.difficultyReason: Part (b) requires fixing Bella to remove rotational repeats, excluding her two neighbouring seats when placing Zoe, then arranging the remaining six people. This routinely adapts the supplied fixed-person method and seating scaffold; part (a) applies the circular-arrangement formula directly.

children.label: a
children.prompt: 10 people sit around a round table. How many ways can this be done?

spec.description: Ten seat markers around an implied circle, with an inner ring on the top marker. Decorative blue is replaced by black outlines.
spec.mathematics: Ten distinct people; one position is fixed to remove rotational repeats.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete unlabelled seating scaffold remains visible.

answer.worked:
Fix the first person; the remaining nine people have $9,8,\ldots,1$ choices.

$$\begin{aligned}N&=1\times9\times8\times7\times6\times5\times4\times3\times2\times1\\&=9!\\&=362\,880\text{ ways}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: 8 people sit around a round table. Bella and Zoe do not want to sit together. How many possible arrangements are there?

spec.description: Eight seat markers around an implied circle, with an inner ring on the top marker. Decorative blue is replaced by black outlines.
spec.mathematics: Fix Bella; exclude her two neighbouring seats when placing Zoe.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete unlabelled seating scaffold remains visible.

answer.worked:
Fix Bella in one position. Of the seven remaining seats, two are beside Bella, so Zoe has five choices. The other six people can be arranged in $6!$ ways.

$$\begin{aligned}N&=1\times5\times6\times5\times4\times3\times2\times1\\&=5\times6!\\&=3600\text{ arrangements}.\end{aligned}$$
